# First mount races the dock swap under SharedWorkers, poisoning updates

## Context

A consumer workspace boots its dock **empty at construct** and swaps the real document in later (`initDocument` after an async licence/session step) — a boot shape the engine's own consumers never exercise (workstation and `examples/dashboard/dock` both seed a real document at construct time). Under `useSharedWorkers: true` in a fresh browser profile, that swap races the initial DOM mount and the workspace comes up wrong **and stays wrong**.

## The Problem

Measured on a live app via the Neural Link + Playwright (fresh Chromium profiles, engine dev tip):

- **Worker truth is perfect**: `get_dock_topology` returns the correct committed `neo.dock.zone.v1` document (two panes placed); the component tree holds exactly the expected instances (`mounted: true`, `hidden: false`).
- **DOM lies**: the row renders `[old center @ full viewport width][empty new-center slot @ exactly the correct width][splitter][edge band]` — the edge band sits at x=2304 in a 1280px viewport, one center-width off-screen. The retained pane never moved into the new projection's slot; the old shell never left.
- **Delta stream stops**: instrumenting every worker-port message on main, ghost boots receive the initial mount plus **one** update batch, then silence. A healthy boot (observed once — the race is timing-sensitive, ~6/7 ghost in fresh profiles, 0/many with dedicated workers) shows the full expected sequence, ending in exactly the batches whose absence produces the ghost: `moveNode <retained tab container> → <new center slot>` and `removeNode <old shell>`.
- **Not self-healing**: a committed `resizeEdgeZone` (verified `applied: true`, document updated) resizes only the center; splitter and band stay frozen at their displaced positions. Every subsequent projection appears poisoned — the page also logs repeating `Uncaught (in promise) undefined` rejections.

## The Architectural Reality

- The consumer path: construct → `dockModel = emptyDocument()` → projection A mounts → async gate → `initDocument()` → `refreshDockWorkspace()` → reconciler stages projection B, retains panes by identity, and swaps child 0 of the dock host.
- `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` already memorializes the failure class this belongs to: the refresh tail carries a `.catch()` because "one rejected re-projection used to poison every later one".
- The ghost DOM containing BOTH the old content and the new shell suggests the **initial mount serialized a mid-staging vdom tree** (old projection + staged shell co-resident), after which the reconciler's deltas — computed against the tree it believed was mounted — target ids/positions that never matched, and each application rejects.
- SharedWorker boot is slower to first mount than dedicated workers (three shared connections + handshakes), which is plausibly what widens the race window from ~never to ~always in fresh profiles.

## Reproducer

1. Engine-only: give `examples/dashboard/dock` the consumer boot shape — construct with an EMPTY document (one empty tabs zone), then apply the real seed via a queued microtask/timeout after construct; set `useSharedWorkers: true`; load in a **fresh** Chromium profile (Playwright `chromium.launch()` per run).
2. Assert: every committed pane's DOM rect lies inside the viewport, and the dock host holds exactly ONE projection subtree.
3. The failing geometry is deterministic enough to assert on: retained pane at full viewport width, its target slot empty at (viewport − band − splitter) width, band fully off-screen.

## The Fix (directions, for the taker to falsify)

- Order the first projection against the mount boundary: `refreshDockWorkspace` awaits the host's mount (or the initial mount awaits an in-flight refresh) so the mount never serializes a staging tree.
- And/or: make the reconciler's swap resilient to a mid-staging mount — re-sync against the actually-mounted tree instead of the assumed one, so a lost/mismatched delta degrades to a full re-projection rather than a poisoned channel.
- The repeating `Uncaught (in promise) undefined` also deserves a name: whatever rejects there should carry a message; silence made this materially harder to find.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The reproducer boots correctly under `useSharedWorkers: true` in fresh profiles (N≥5 consecutive runs).
- [ ] A regression test covers the empty-construct → async-swap boot shape under shared workers.
- [ ] Post-boot committed operations re-project all zones (the resize-moves-only-center symptom is asserted against).
- [ ] The formerly-`undefined` rejection path rejects with a named error.
- [ ] Dedicated-worker boots unchanged (existing suites green).

## Out of Scope

- The consumer's own boot-shape choices (empty-at-construct is legitimate; licence-gated catalogs require it).
- The workstation FLIP/pooled-grid reports (#17871, #17872) — possibly the same poisoned-projection family from a different trigger; verify against this fix but do not assume.
